6d26acd9bcddb560: PUTRAJAYA: The Election Commission (EC) said there is currently no proposal to increase the number of parliamentary constituencies in Sarawak, contrary to a local newspaper report linking the matter to discussions on the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).

EC secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus said the report cited a purported document on the proposed redelineation of Sarawak's parliamentary constituencies, which the newspaper claimed to have obtained.

"The EC has only prepared recommendations for the Seventh Sarawak Electoral Constituency Redelineation Review, which are currently on public display throughout this month," he said in a statement today.
Khairul Shahril advised the newspaper to refer to authentic and accurate information on the redelineation exercise through the EC's official portal or statements.

The local Malay-language newspaper had earlier reported that the proposed redelineation exercise would see the number of parliamentary constituencies in Sarawak increase from 31 to 46, citing a document purportedly outlining the exercise.
92f4a4cb413e94e5: NAGOYA: Thailand's Puripol Boonson broke his own Asian Games record to win gold in the men's 100m in 9.90 seconds in Nagoya on Friday.

China's Chen Yujie won the women's 100m in a Games-record 11.06sec to relegate the Hangzhou gold medallist, Singapore's Shanti Pereira (11.21), to the silver. Bahrain's Edidiong Odiong took bronze in 11.33.
The 20-year-old Puripol's semi-final run of 9.91sec had eclipsed the 9.92 sec by China's Su Bingtian at the 2018 edition in Jakarta.
But the Thai shaved another 100th off that in the final to finish well clear of the Omani pair of Ali Al-Balushi (10.04) and Malham Al-Balushi (10.11).
Puripol's and Chen's exploits were watched by a sparse crowd with the Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium only about a quarter full.
It was Thailand's first men's 100m gold medal since Suchart Jairsuraparp won on home soil at the 1978 Bangkok Games.
Bahrain's Birhanu Balew won his fourth Asian Games gold medal when he crossed the line first in the men's 10,000 metres in 28min 27.51sec.
The Ethiopian-born distance runner added to his 5,000m golds in Jakarta 2018 and Hangzhou three years ago, where he also won the 10,000m.
Now he will chase a fifth Asian Games gold in the 5,000 metres on Tuesday.
"I think that after the 5,000 metres, Inshallah, I will get another gold medal, the fifth," said Balew who won the Diamond League 5,000m title this year.-AFP
812dcb17f5c26838: NAGOYA: Shereen Samson Vallabouy's mission to defend her Asian Games bronze medal ended in heartbreak after she was eliminated in the first round of the women's 400m event here today.
Shereen had to settle for a fourth-place finish in the third heat after clocking 54.03 seconds at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, which was not enough to secure a place in the final.
The heat was won by Iranian runner Zahra Zarei Manoujan in 52.00s, followed by Uzbekistan's Jonbibi Hukmova in second place (52.05s), whilst India's Prachi finished third (53.46s).
Only the top two runners from each heat and the next two fastest overall times qualified for the final.
Shereen claimed bronze at the Hangzhou Games on 52.58s. She is also the national record holder with a time of 51.80s.
Shereen admitted her disappointment at failing to replicate her achievement from three years ago, but stressed that she had given everything in the race.
"It wasn't what I hoped for. My time wasn't where I wanted it to be, and I was far off my best," she said.
"Honestly, I gave it everything I had. I can't blame myself, and I need to review the race with my coach to figure out what happened."
Shereen added that she must bounce back and move forward in her athletics career.
"Yes, of course I'm disappointed. I won't lie, I'm sad, but honestly, I gave it my all.
"This just isn't my year. I need to come back stronger and keep moving forward," she said.
Meanwhile, men's 400m runner Umar Osman also failed to reach the final in his event after finishing sixth in the second heat on 46.91s.
That heat was won by India's V. Thennarasu in 45.27s, followed by Ammar Ibrahim of Qatar (45.31s), whilst Sri Lanka's Kalinga Kumarge placed third (45.74s).
9fbcdf55b70a82ed: KUANTAN: Pas has begun preparations to contest the Kuala Sentul and Lepar state seats, which were won by Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the 15th general election (GE15).

Pahang Pas commissioner Datuk Rosli Abdul Jabar said there was no longer an alliance between Pas and Bersatu following the split between the two parties, while the assemblymen for both seats now support the Barisan Nasional (BN) state government.
"During the last general election, both constituencies were won under the PN logo. The split between Pas and Bersatu means any party has the right to contest the seats.

"Since the previous victories were secured under the PN banner, Pas is also entitled to field candidates in the constituencies in the 16th general election (GE16). Furthermore, a large part of the machinery that worked towards PN's victories in both constituencies comprised Pas members and supporters," he said in a Facebook post today.
Rosli said Pahang Pas had already begun its groundwork, with several programmes carried out and more planned.
"Everything is in place for Pas Pahang to contest both seats, including its election machinery, funding, schedules and the best candidates. All preparations have been made in detail.

"Pas is confident that voters in Kuala Sentul and Lepar will side with the party, based on the strong commitment shown by all Pas state assemblymen and members of parliament in Pahang in carrying out their mandates despite limited funding," he said.

Following GE15, Pahang PN had 17 elected representatives — 15 from Pas and two from Bersatu. The two Bersatu assemblymen are Lepar assemblyman Mohd Yazid Mohd Yunus and Kuala Sentul assemblyman Datuk Jasri Jamaludin.
However, last month, Yazid and Jasri pledged their support for
Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail and backed his administration until GE16.
Lepar is under the Umno-led Paya Besar parliamentary constituency, while Kuala Sentul falls under the Pas-led Maran parliamentary constituency.
In GE15, BN and PN each won 17 seats in the Pahang Legislative Assembly, while Pakatan Harapan secured eight, giving the 42-member assembly its current composition.

4a8058413e677802: KUALA LUMPUR: Peranan Malaysia sebagai fasilitator amat diperlukan dalam proses damai Bangsamoro dan negara ini perlu meneruskan penglibatannya, kata Pengerusi Panel Pelaksana Damai Barisan Pembebasan Islam Moro (MILF) Mohagher Iqbal.
Beliau berkata, MILF dan kerajaan Filipina mempunyai tahap kepercayaan yang tinggi terhadap sikap tidak memihak Malaysia dalam proses damai itu.

“Peranan Malaysia sebagai fasilitator amat diperlukan. Malaysia ialah perantara yang jujur dan sejak 2001, negara ini telah bersama-sama kedua-dua pihak dalam proses ini, menangani serta mengatasi pelbagai halangan sepanjang perjalanan.
“Jadi, tiada sebab mengapa Malaysia tidak harus terus menjadi negara fasilitator. Malaysia telah membuktikan keupayaannya,” katanya ketika sidang media pada Jumaat.

Mohagher berkata, Malaysia memainkan peranan penting sebagai fasilitator dalam perjanjian antara kerajaan Filipina dan MILF, termasuk Perjanjian Rangka Kerja mengenai Bangsamoro dan Perjanjian Komprehensif mengenai Bangsamoro (CAB).
CAB yang dimeterai pada 2014 membuka jalan kepada penggubalan Undang-Undang Organik Bangsamoro dan penubuhan Pihak Berkuasa Peralihan Bangsamoro.

“Berdasarkan rekodnya, saya berpendapat Malaysia perlu dan mesti terus terlibat dalam proses damai kerana kedua-dua pihak, khususnya MILF, mempunyai tahap kepercayaan yang sangat tinggi terhadap sikap tidak memihak Malaysia,” kata Mohagher.
Beliau berkata, Malaysia kekal sebagai faktor penting dalam membawa proses damai itu ke arah penyelesaian muktamad menerusi Perjanjian Penamatan.
“Saya berani mengatakan bahawa tanpa Malaysia sebagai perantara yang jujur, saya tidak fikir kita mampu sampai sejauh ini," katanya.
“Malaysia telah bersama-sama dalam proses damai ini sejak 2001 dan kami berharap Malaysia akan terus menjadi fasilitator rundingan ini sehingga Perjanjian Penamatan dimeterai."
Terdahulu, Mohagher menghadiri Mesyuarat Khas Panel Pelaksana Damai GPH-MILF mengenai pelaksanaan CAB.
Delegasi kerajaan Filipina diketuai Penasihat Presiden mengenai Keamanan, Rekonsiliasi dan Perpaduan, Setiausaha Mel Senen Sarmiento, manakala Mohagher mengetuai delegasi MILF.
Fasilitator proses damai Zulkifli Zainal Abidin turut hadir.
c1f6b597c762f52a: Microsoft has admitted that some Windows 11 virtual desktops may fail to load after sign-in, leaving users staring at a black screen until they launch Explorer manually. The glitch affects devices running the August 2026 non-security preview update or later releases and, according to Microsoft, "has been primarily observed on Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) hosts, using FSLogix." Windows Explorer crashes may appear in the affected device's Application event log. Users can temporarily recover the desktop by opening Task Manager and running explorer.exe as a new task. Microsoft has also issued a Known Issue Rollback (KIR) that administrators can deploy through Group Policy. This disables the offending change until a permanent fix arrives. "We are working on a resolution for this issue, and it will be released in a future Windows update," the company said. This is distinct from another problem introduced by the same August preview update, which replaced some customized desktop backgrounds with solid black. Microsoft fixed that in September, but has not explained precisely what causes this latest failure. It said only that the problem "appears to occur more frequently with some existing user profiles." That will be of limited comfort to users glumly firing up Task Manager to launch their desktops manually. Windows 11 versions 26H1, 25H2, and 24H2 are affected. Microsoft does not list Windows 10 or Windows Server among the affected platforms. The stream of problems introduced by Microsoft's August and September updates is becoming relentless, undermining the company's claims that Windows is getting better. Quality improvement promises made earlier this year by Windows chief Pavan Davuluri are ringing increasingly hollow. If this is how Microsoft plans to "win back" its fans, as Satya Nadella said it must, the response may well be: thanks, but no thanks. ®

ef9d39805e41d38a: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Bar will file a challenge against the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Najib Razak while continuing its appeal against the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s 2024 decision to halve his jail term and reduce his fine in the SRC International case.

Its president, Anand Raj, said Malaysia does not have a formal legal framework for house arrest, pointing also to previous statements by Justice Alice Loke and home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail saying as much.
“From our research to date, there appear to be no standard operating procedures or guidelines in place for house arrests.
“A whole new ecosystem of rules and procedures would be required for house arrests,” he said in a statement today.

On Sept 18, Najib was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of a six-year jail sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and other conditions.

The 73-year-old has been serving a six-year sentence at Kajang prison after the pardons board halved his original 12-year sentence in February 2024. The original RM210 million fine was also reduced to RM50 million.
The Bar's ongoing appeal seeks to quash the 2024 decision and obtain a declaration that it was unlawful, unconstitutional and void.
On Jan 7 next year, the Court of Appeal will deliver a ruling on the Bar's appeal against the High Court's previous refusal to grant leave for judicial review.

Meanwhile, Anand questioned Umno's donation drive to collect the funds needed for Najib's RM50 million fine, given the reported return of RM114 million in seized cash and assets to Najib and the party.

“It is unclear why Najib has reportedly said that most of his assets are frozen when more than enough of his previously seized assets appear to have been returned to cover the RM50 million fine, without the need for a public fundraiser.
“Perhaps there may be other assets (which were not seized circa May 2018) that may have been frozen, but this is not clear, nor have any details been made available publicly,” he said.

The RM114 million was seized in a raid on his apartment days after the 2018 general election. It had been the subject of an unsuccessful forfeiture proceeding brought by the government before reportedly being returned to him in 2021.

84145acc316f679c: MELAKA: A former army corporal was acquitted and discharged by the Ayer Keroh magistrate's court here today of 17 charges, including 15 counts of molesting a male recruit at Terendak Camp in 2023.
Magistrate Uthman Abd Ghani made the decision after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against the accused, Mohd Amanah Habhijullah, 38.
He said the dates and times for each charge had not been specified, leaving the prosecution case heavily reliant on the evidence of the complainant, who was also the first prosecution witness (SP1).
"The court found that SP1 could not recall the dates of the incidents, while the prosecution alleged that the 15 offences occurred between August and October 2023.
"SP1 could only recall one date, Oct 14, 2023, after referring to the police report," he said when delivering his brief judgment at the end of the prosecution's case today.
Uthman said there were discrepancies between SP1's police report and his testimony in court, particularly concerning the accused's actions after the alleged incident on Oct 14, 2023.

He said the court also found discrepancies in the evidence relating to two charges involving causing injury, including the allegation that the accused hit SP1 with a broomstick and kicked him in the chest on Oct 15, 2023.

According to Uthman, the testimonies of several witnesses concerning the incident differed, including on whether SP1 was hit on the head, whether the broomstick broke and whether there was any bleeding.
"For the 17th charge, there were also discrepancies concerning the presence of another witness at the scene.
"SP1 initially said there was another witness, but after the police report was referred to, he said only he and the accused were at the location," he said.

Uthman said although SP1 had experienced trauma and depression following his relationship with the accused, the prosecution case was still riddled with discrepancies and reasonable doubt, and was not supported by sufficient evidence in law.

The court subsequently acquitted and discharged Mohd Amanah of all 17 charges, ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case and that it would not be safe to call on the accused to enter his defence.
Deputy public prosecutor Syauqi Mardia Baharudin prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer S Daniel.
After the proceedings, Mohd Amanah appeared emotional and expressed gratitude over the court's decision.
He described the case as defamatory.
"...For 2 years and 4 months, I was disappointed because I was accused. That is why I wanted to fight this case because I knew I was being accused by him (the complainant) without evidence," he said.
A total of 11 prosecution witnesses testified during the trial.
On March 15, 2024, media reported that the accused was first charged in court with 17 offences, including 15 counts of molesting a male army recruit.

d7b0c192729f51ce: NEW DELHI, Sept 25 — A string of rape cases in India has reignited debate over women’s safety and raised questions about why sweeping legal reforms and tougher punishments have failed to curb sexual violence.
Hundreds of students marched through the streets of New Delhi on Wednesday, shouting slogans and holding placards demanding stronger safety measures following the latest high-profile case.
In that incident on Monday, three men posing as police officers allegedly gang-raped a 17-year-old girl in a public park in the heart of the capital city, according to authorities.
The case evokes the 2012 gang rape and murder of a 23-year-old physical therapy student on a bus, which triggered nationwide protests and led to more robust laws against sexual violence.
But campaigners say those changes, which included a broadening of the definition of sexual offences and the introduction of stronger punishments for rape, have proven inadequate.
“Nobody is working on the actual solution, which is the mindset change,” women’s rights activist Yogita Bhayana told AFP.
“The mentality (is still) that it is a woman’s fault to be out of home late, or men policing women if they are seen with another man,” she said.
“It is outrageous that society still thinks this way.”

India recorded an average of 80 rape cases per day in 2024, according to the latest available official data. That compares with around 68 per day in 2012, the last year before the stronger laws came in.
Activists say the true number of sexual assaults is likely far higher because many victims never file a report, often fearing stigma in a deeply patriarchal society.
Lack of enforcement

The alleged assault on Monday followed the rape and murder of a 16-year-old girl whose body was found by police in a decomposed state, and the alleged rape of a 17-year-old girl by a bus driver and a conductor who offered her a lift during heavy rain.

Both cases occurred in recent weeks in Delhi — often called India’s “rape capital” — but other regions are not immune, with a video that surfaced this month showing a teenage girl being sexually assaulted in the eastern state of Bihar.
Each case has brought arrests, political condemnation and a public outcry.

After the watershed 2012 case — the woman is known nationally as “Nirbhaya” or “Fearless”, as Indian law does not allow the press to publish a rape victim’s name — the government expanded the criminal definitions of penetration and consent.
Gang rape became punishable by at least 20 years in prison, and the death sentence was introduced for repeat rape offenders.
Lawyers and activists say the challenge lies in enforcement.

Overstretched police forces and courts lack the means to investigate cases thoroughly enough, hindering the reforms’ impacts, criminal lawyer Shilpi Jain, who has represented survivors of sexual violence, told AFP.
“The problem is not in the law but with the people who are implementing it,” she said.
“Overworked judges. Overworked cops. One police station handles 200,000 to 300,000 people. How will it work? This is a vicious cycle.”
India’s conviction rate for rape has remained largely stable since 2012, hovering at around a quarter of all cases that make it to trial.
But the criminal justice system struggles with a vast case backlog.
Less than 10 per cent of the more than 200,000 rape cases before the courts in 2024 were actually completed, according to official data.
“An average rape case takes seven to eight years. If the case goes to the Supreme Court, then 20 years, so criminals lose fear of law and victims lose hope,” Jain said.
For gender rights activist Poonam Muttreja, legal reforms alone cannot solve a problem rooted in social attitudes and inequality.
Deep-seated cultural taboos and political resistance have hampered the effectiveness of government programmes to raise awareness of sexual violence, experts say.
“Prevention must begin much before a crime is committed: in homes, schools, communities, digital spaces and police systems,” Muttreja said. — AFP

919c58cc315e41dc: NEW YORK, Sept 25 — Nepal’s catastrophic flooding last month “was a warning to the world” about the rising dangers of climate change, Prime Minister Balendra Shah told the United Nations yesterday, urging countries to step up to help his country adapt.

Addressing the General Assembly in sunglasses during its high-level week, Shah said a warming climate was “destabilising the fragile Himalayan ecology,” melting permafrost and glaciers and accelerating hazards.

The nation suffered one of the worst catastrophes in its history late last month when a tsunami-like flood, triggered by a high-altitude glacial mountain collapse along the Nepal-China border, cut a swathe of destruction.
More than 1,400 people died, 6,000 are still missing, and the economic devastation runs in the billions of dollars.

Scientists from the World Weather Attribution have described the event as a “compound crisis” in which local geological instability combined with long-term warming has led to glacier retreat and permafrost thaw.
“Nepal contributes less than 0.1 per cent of global greenhouse gas emission. We did not create this crisis, yet we are paying for it,” he said.

Shah urged the international community to help bear the cost of helping his country adapt to climate change, because “Nepal cannot build resilience alone against a crisis made worse by the failure of global governance.”

He proposed to create what he called a “Himalaya Climate Resilience Mechanism,” which would include Nepal and its neighbours India and China, and allow them to share satellite data and expertise, monitor glacial lakes and strengthen joint early warning systems.
A 36-year-old ex-rapper, Shah swept to power six months ago on a wave of youth-led anti-corruption protests, buoyed by optimism for change.
But the disaster has pushed climate diplomacy to the centre of his premiership, overshadowing the anti-corruption agenda.

A general view of the damaged suspension bridge in the aftermath of the August 26 flash flood, at Taruka in Nepal’s Nuwakot district September 24, 2026. The tsunami-like flood that cut a swathe of destruction through Nepal on August 26 has left the Himalayan nation grappling with heavy losses and mounting reconstruction needs. — AFP pic

Nepal has asked the UN’s Loss and Damage fund for US$20 million (RM81.5 million) in aid, the maximum allowed, but a tiny fraction of what it needs — a preliminary assessment by the government has placed the cost of the disaster at US$5 billion.
The fund, established in 2022 in the aftermath of catastrophic floods in Pakistan, has yet to make even its first disbursement, and observers see Nepal as a key test of its credibility.
Earlier this week, the United States pledged an additional US$31 million in new flood recovery support.
Nepal’s foreign minister Shisir Khanal told AFP that the G7 informally promised support at a meeting on Wednesday, and Britain has also vowed to help. — AFP
e2d668411af0584a: GENEVA, Sept 25 — Gaza is suffering the world’s worst economic crisis ever recorded, with nine in 10 businesses destroyed and hundreds of thousands of people unemployed, a top UN development agency warned yesterday.
Israel’s military offensive sparked by Hamas militants’ attack in October 2023 devastated the territory of two million people before a patchy ceasefire was announced in October 2025.
“The collapse of the economy of Gaza is the world’s most severe economic crisis on record,” said Pedro Manuel Moreno, acting secretary-general of the UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD).
“It has wiped out decades of development and generated an acute economic crisis for its people,” he told reporters in Geneva as the organisation released a new report.
It said 92 per cent of Gaza’s “economic establishments have been damaged or destroyed”.
The territory’s daily per capita GDP is US$0.58 (RM2.37) a day, the report said. Prices are 274 per cent higher than in 2022.
Israel’s military offensive killed more than 73,000 people, according to the territory’s health ministry under Hamas authority, whose figures are regarded as reliable by the United Nations.
It displaced virtually the entire population and damaged or destroyed most of its buildings.
Before October 2023, “two out of three Gazans were poor. Today, everyone in Gaza is multidimensionally poor,” said Mutasim Elagraa, UNCTAD’s coordinator for assistance to the Palestinians.
Industrial activity and agricultural production have fallen by 94 per cent, with only 1.5 per cent of arable land accessible, forcing “total dependence on humanitarian food aid”, Elagraa said.
According to the report, the conflict has destroyed hundreds of thousands of jobs, leaving more than 90 per cent of Gaza’s working-age population unemployed.
The report also detailed an economic and financial crisis in the occupied West Bank, citing “reduced access to land and natural resources linked to (Israeli) settlement expansion”.
The Palestinian government has borrowed heavily from local banks, drawn on the Palestinian pension fund and owes money to private contractors, Elagraa said.
The Palestinian territories risk a “banking collapse”, he warned. The “political and social and humanitarian consequences will be immense”. — AFP

ea0d14f119a00611: NEW YORK: UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres warned on Thursday that the work and mandate of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (UNRWA) were in jeopardy, Palestine News and Information Agency (WAFA) reported.

Speaking at the annual ministerial meeting on the agency's work during High-Level Week in New York, Guterres said UNRWA continued to operate under “extraordinary pressure”, with nearly 400 members of its workforce in Gaza killed and hundreds of its premises in the Occupied Palestinian Territory rendered “inaccessible, severely damaged, or utterly destroyed”.
“These actions are wholly unacceptable and inconsistent with Israel’s obligations under international law, including the UN Charter,” he said.

Despite the highly challenging environment, Guterres said UNRWA continued to provide essential public services to Palestinian refugees, but its work and mandate from the General Assembly were now in “jeopardy”.

Nearly two years ago, the Israeli Knesset passed legislation banning the UN agency from operating on Israeli territory, including East Jerusalem, and prohibiting Israeli officials from cooperating with UNRWA.

The Israeli government seized and began demolishing UNRWA’s main compound in Jerusalem last January. The UN and several states maintain that the laws passed by the Knesset breach Israel’s obligations under the UN Charter and Security Council Resolution 2730 on the protection of humanitarian personnel.

According to Guterres, the agency has been excluded from coordination meetings with Israeli authorities over humanitarian operations in the Gaza Strip and elsewhere, while Israel no longer grants visas to its staff, and UNRWA personnel have been subjected to intimidation.
He said UNRWA also continued to face a severe financial crisis, with a cash shortfall of US$100 million putting operations at risk and threatening the welfare of millions of Palestinian refugees.
Guterres called on member states to take immediate action, saying UNRWA’s capacity to operate was “seriously imperilled” and regional stability was at “stake”.
He said continued Israeli attacks were killing an average of four people a day, “a quarter of them children”, while international law was being “brazenly violated”.
“The resumption of assistance since the ceasefire was announced last October has brought some relief – but conditions remain intolerable,” Guterres said.
He said Israeli settler attacks and efforts to expand settlements in the West Bank had pushed Palestinians to “breaking point” and posed a threat to the two-state solution.
Amid the volatility, Guterres said UNRWA remained a “critical stabilising presence” and a lifeline for many Palestinian refugees.

a8bc695471ca7e97: The US government wants to join Elon Musk and X's legal challenge to the European Commission's €120 million fine against the social media platform. The Commission issued its first fine under the Digital Services Act (DSA) in December 2025, finding that X had breached transparency rules through its paid blue checkmarks, advertising repository, and restrictions on researchers' access to public data. X owner Elon Musk described the decision as "crazy" and "insane" in a Xeet, and compared the "woke" Commission to "Stasi commissars," combining two rather different authoritarian references. Before issuing a response, he shared the comments made by FCC chair Brendan Carr, who accused "Europe" of "fining a successful US tech company for being a successful US tech company." "Europe is taxing Americans to subsidize a continent held back by Europe's own suffocating regulations," Carr added. US politicians also rallied around Musk. Senator Ted Cruz called the fine "an abomination" and an attack on American free speech. The US government has now applied to intervene in the cases brought by Musk and X Internet and X Holdings, supporting their attempts to annul the Commission's decision. Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate accused the Commission of regulatory overreach against US companies beyond its jurisdiction. "The European Commission inappropriately attempted to expand its regulatory authority to reach American companies not present or operating within its jurisdiction," he said. "We will not tolerate the European Commission engaging in regulatory overreach to try and control American engines of innovation and economic growth." The Justice Department said it has "significant concerns" about how the Commission determined which people and companies constituted the provider of X's digital service. It intends to argue that the decision conflicts with accepted limits on extraterritorial jurisdiction and the principle that companies are ordinarily legally distinct from their owners and shareholders. It was especially concerned that the Commission's approach "extended legal scrutiny to Mr Musk himself as a private individual" and implicated other US companies under his control. According to the DoJ, the Commission found the parties jointly and severally liable for the €120 million fine and calculated it using the worldwide turnover of the corporate group ultimately controlled by Musk. The US government argues that allowing this approach to stand could have broader consequences for American-owned digital platforms operating in the EU. The DoJ stated: "If the approach in the European Commission Decision is upheld, this may have significant implications for 'very large online platforms' and other similar entities operating in the digital services sector within the EU, many of which are domiciled (at parent level) within the United States. "The United States looks forward to the opportunity to address these concerns and issues in detail before the General Court." Musk bought Twitter in 2022 and subsequently replaced its identity-based verification system with a subscription offering. Blue checkmarks, previously awarded by Twitter to accounts it considered authentic and notable, became available to paying users without equivalent identity checks. The change swiftly produced impersonation and spam, and the Commission concluded that presenting those accounts as "verified" amounted to deceptive design. The Commission also found that X's advertising repository lacked required information and imposed access barriers that prevented effective scrutiny of advertisements. Separately, it said X placed unnecessary obstacles in the way of researchers seeking public platform data. The violations behind the EU fine are separate from matters under investigation in the UK, including X's handling of illegal hate speech and terrorist content flowing through its feeds and Grok's highly controversial nudifying functionality. The Commission has since accepted X's plan to address the advertising repository and researcher access violations. The €120 million penalty and the legal theory used to calculate and impose it remain the subjects of the challenges now before the General Court – and, if its application succeeds, of an intervention by the US government. ®
2a9ca64c5f5ea2c5: SCROLL through any local EV forum or social media comment section today, and you will find a consistent chorus of anger.

When the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry tightened its regulatory stance with protective walls - such as the minimum RM200,000 CIF threshold and 180 kW motor output floors for fully imported (CBU) electric vehicles - the digital reaction was swift and predictable.
The government was accused of shielding legacy dinosaurs, choking the green technology revolution, and locking everyday Malaysians out of affordable mobility.

From the perspective of an individual consumer grappling with the cost-of-living squeeze, that frustration makes complete sense. Who wouldn't want a silent, high-tech, zero-emission vehicle at a sub-RM150,000 price point?
When the low-price bonanza suddenly disappears just as a significant portion of the market is starting to get on board, the instinctive reaction is to blast the policy as bureaucratic gatekeeping.
The optics certainly support the anger.

Then last week, Thailand - which had previously been very bullish on electric vehicles - decided to slam the brakes on imports as well, instituting higher tariffs and even stricter local content requirements for vehicles assembled within their borders.
The "Detroit of Southeast Asia" is fast looking like a manufacturing hub under siege, caught off guard by the faster-than-expected transition toward battery electric vehicles.
As a nation with hardly any proven petroleum reserves, Thailand's push for electrification seemed logical, commendable even.
But three years after the starter gun was fired in 2023, the situation for their domestic automotive industry is looking quite grim.

By June this year, BEVs and hybrids accounted to 55 per cent of all car sales - a number beyond the imagination of policymakers who aimed for 30 per cent of locally made cars to be zero-emission vehicles by 2030.
Once that 30 per cent target was breached last year, and it became clear that the vast majority of ZEVs sold were imported from China, the government knew they had to change the game.
Faced with monumental excess capacity at home, Chinese automakers were forced to export.

They took advantage of whatever state financial incentives they could secure to chase foreign reserves, and went to town with it. This resulted in record car exports from China in 2025, and the trend shows no sign of slowing down.
Australia is now awash with Chinese brands, dominating the EV segment so thoroughly that nearly all non-Tesla competitors have retreated.

Mighty Volkswagen is so battered by the global tsunami that they are looking to cut 100,000 jobs at home and abroad. Things are so bad they sold off Bugatti and are reportedly contemplating letting Ducati go - selling their crown jewels just to keep the lights on.
Thailand and Malaysia have very little by way of home-grown technology to compete with China.
Yet Germany, which essentially dominated automotive engineering for the last century, is now begging Brussels to erect tariff walls just so it can catch its breath.
To be honest, it's hard to overstate the tectonic shift happening in the global auto industry right now, and Thailand's sudden pivot is merely a shockwave from that wider tremor. Any nation with a
domestic supply chain is feeling the heat, starting with the smaller players - local vendors supplying minor components to Tier-1 suppliers.

These outfits, running on razor-thin margins with fewer than 50 workers, can weather a few stormy months. But if orders keep shrinking with no sign of recovery, layoffs become inevitable, with the sobering knowledge that rehiring skilled hands later will not be easy.

Thailand has far more to lose than Malaysia. Their supply chain runs much deeper, and vastly more livelihoods rely on the sector because their installed capacity sits around 2 million units a year - more than double ours.

Furthermore, Thai factories function primarily as heavy export manufacturing bases. With Japanese mainstays like Honda, Mitsubishi, Nissan, and Mazda under global pressure, Thai production output is forced to contract to match market reality.

Malaysia's car factories, by contrast, feed over 90 per cent of their output straight to the domestic market. Because our local components industry calculates local content differently than the Thais, our immediate shocks will be smaller, though still painful.
As our domestic market surged post-pandemic, our automotive component trade deficit ballooned from RM15 billion in 2020 to RM39 billion last year.
Yes, we have local assembly, but not nearly enough true local content. If August sales figures for Proton e.MAS are any indication, the market is finally warming up to battery power.

But looking at Proton alone, it is clear they massively underestimated the shift. When they launched their EV assembly line late last year capped at 20,000 units annually - a paltry number I pointed out at the time - they insisted they had expansion plans to 40,000.
Even that feels conservative. With the e.Mas brand pulling in numbers tracking toward the Saga, they are severely straining against demand.
In the short term, expect them to hunt for excess capacity wherever they can find it. In the medium term, trees are going to have to come down for major factory expansion in Tanjung Malim.
And then we will hit the brick wall of local content.

The uncomfortable truth is that we do not have the manufacturing depth to even come close to fulfilling true local content requirements, even if brands genuinely want to cross every T and dot every I.

For too long, the local component ecosystem has been living a polite fiction. In a desire to accommodate domestic players, authorities allowed modules assembled using foreign child parts to be counted as local content. Decades of such lenient enforcement mean we can no longer even properly enforce our own industrial rules.
So, as we grandstand about defending the local industry, I am haunted by the image of Pak Kaduk - the classic folktale figure who traded away his winning fighting cock right before the main match.
When his former bird won, he cheered wildly, forgetting entirely that the champion had changed hands before the bell rang.
There is still time, but very little.
We need an honest, brutal assessment of our local component suppliers and their true technological capabilities before deciding how to navigate the wild west of the EV transition.
Otherwise, the ministry and enforcement agencies will simply keep inventing creative loopholes to preserve the illusion of policy compliance, while we pretend that all is well.
The rock is global geopolitics that we cannot control. The hard place is entirely of our own making.

107427b1928022f2: PETALING JAYA: Golongan muda di Malaysia mahu kerajaan menyediakan bantuan tunai secara langsung dalam Belanjawan 2027, menurut Exco Pemuda PKR Noor Amelia Zainabila Zaiffri.
Noor Amelia berkata, pandangan itu berasaskan maklum balas golongan itu sepanjang dua sesi dialog awam tahun lepas.

“Secara jujurnya, apa yang mereka perlukan ialah bantuan tunai. Berilah baucar buku atau kad sekalipun, bantuan tunai tetap jadi pilihan,” katanya dalam episod terbaru siri Kena Soal di podcast Keluar Sekejap kendalian Iman Irfan Yahya.
Episod ke-12 siri Kena Soal itu diterbitkan di bawah inisiatif Future Speaks dengan kerjasama FMT.
Menurut Noor Amelia, persepsi serupa turut wujud dalam isu perumahan, apabila insentif kerajaan dilihat sekadar meringankan beban kewangan pembeli muda, bukannya sebagai bentuk bantuan langsung.
Beliau memberi contoh pengecualian penuh duti setem bagi pemilikan rumah pertama berharga sehingga RM500,000.

Sementara itu, ahli Puteri Umno Shamellya Norazizi menyambut baik bantuan kewangan untuk pembeli rumah muda, namun mengingatkan golongan berkenaan agar memikirkan selama mana mereka akan bergantung pada inisiatif sedemikian.

“Kerajaan memang bertanggungjawab salur bantuan dan wajar berbuat demikian, tetapi kita sebagai rakyat Malaysia juga perlu bertanya kepada diri sendiri: Sampai bila kita mahu bergantung (pada bantuan)?”
Shamellya yang juga bekas ketua penerangan Puteri Umno turut bimbang dengan kecenderungan belia berdepan hutang, khususnya melalui skim beli-sekarang-bayar-kemudian (BNPL).
Gen Z tidak lagi utamakan beli rumah?

Menyentuh isu perumahan, Noor Amelia berkata, pemilikan rumah tidak lagi semestinya menjadi keutamaan Generasi Z, dengan sebahagiannya memilih menyewa atas faktor mobiliti pekerjaan atau belum bersedia untuk berkeluarga.

Beliau berkata, kadar deposit yang tinggi turut menjadi kekangan lain, memandangkan segelintir anak muda tidak mampu menampung kos pendahuluan rumah serta memberi komitmen kepada pinjaman sehingga 35 tahun.

Bagaimanapun, beliau menegaskan, ini tidak bermakna kerajaan wajar membiarkan golongan muda terus menyewa tanpa had masa, sambil merujuk perumahan mampu milik, skim sewa untuk milik (RTO) dan jaminan kredit sebagai langkah membantu mereka memiliki rumah.

Sementara itu, Shamellya berkata, pengaruh media sosial serta kecenderungan membandingkan diri dengan rakan sebaya memberi tekanan kepada anak muda untuk mengejar kediaman dan gaya hidup di luar kemampuan mereka.

Justeru, beliau menggesa golongan itu mempertimbangkan rumah mampu milik sebagai permulaan dan mengutamakan simpanan, berbanding menanggung beban hutang berlebihan semata-mata mahu bersaing dengan orang lain.

5e0930e77c362016: TOOWNSVILLE: A last-minute header from Brazilian substitute Rayan salvaged a 1-1 draw with Australia in a thrilling international friendly in Townsville on Friday.
Rayan headed the ball home in the 95th minute to deny the hosts what would have been only their second win over the South American giants.
It was a fitting result from two evenly matched teams who gave everything in front of a sell-out crowd in the North Queensland city.
A superb free kick from Australian youngster Nestory Irankunda had looked enough to give the Socceroos an upset win.

With the two sides locked at 0-0 midway through the second half, Irankunda stepped up and drilled his free kick over the defensive wall into the net, leaving Brazil keeper Hugo Souza rooted to the spot.
But Brazil came out and dominated against an increasingly defensive Australian outfit and were rewarded seconds before full-time.
With both teams looking to rebuild after early exits from this year's World Cup, it was the Socceroos who seized the early advantage.
They dominated possession and territory, attacking with width and finding plenty of space on both sides.
Midfielder Connor Metcalfe went close in just the third minute before an Irankunda bullet forced a good save from Souza.
Brazil weathered the storm and began to get into the game, looking increasingly dangerous through in-form Barcelona striker Raphinha and Chelsea forward Estevao.
Raphinha had a good chance with a header straight to Australian keeper Patrick Beach after 20 minutes before Estevao forced a great save from Beach five minutes later.
The Brazil dominance appeared to have paid off in the 46th minute when Estevao scored, but a VAR review saw the goal ruled out due to an earlier foul on Australian captain Harry Soutar.
The second half saw much of the same, with Brazil controlling the centre and the Socceroos finding space out wide.
The visitors were just edging the match, and it seemed only a matter of time before they scored, but they were shocked by Irankunda's superb free kick.
The Socceroos defended furiously and looked to have held out for the win, but a last-minute corner saw Rayan's header just too powerful for Beach to hold out.
c6b763a9696ea461: KUALA LUMPUR: Yinson Holdings Bhd and MISC Bhd say talks on a potential privatisation of Yinson are ongoing, with the indicative offer price maintained at RM2.35 a share.
In separate Bursa Malaysia filings on Friday, the companies said the proposed deal would be carried out through a scheme of arrangement under Section 366 of the Companies Act 2016.
However, the deal is still subject to further discussions and negotiations, the signing of definitive agreements, a final offer price, as well as regulatory and other required approvals.
Both companies stressed that there is no certainty the talks will result in a deal.
Last month, Yinson said it had received a letter from Yinson Legacy Sdn Bhd the investment vehicle of executive chairman Lim Han Weng and his family.
The letter confirmed that Yinson Legacy was in talks with MISC and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) to take Yinson private.
If an agreement is reached, MISC and Yinson Legacy would acquire the 55.2 per cent of Yinson shares not already held by Yinson Legacy and parties acting in concert with it.
EPF would retain its existing effective stake in Yinson.
Lim and his family hold a combined 27.68 per cent stake, while EPF owns 17.09 per cent. Retirement Fund Inc, better known as KWAP, holds another 6.7 per cent.
Following completion, MISC and Yinson Legacy are expected to hold equal stakes in Yinson.
Yinson operates eight floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessels, with operations spanning Southeast Asia, South America and Africa.
MISC, which is 51 per cent owned by Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), has six FPSOs and six other vessels operating in Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and Brazil.
Yinson also has 557 megawatts of renewable energy assets, with another 148MW under construction in India, Peru and New Zealand.
The group also operates electric vehicle charging stations in Malaysia and Singapore.
8c8b4005cf309816: KUALA LUMPUR: The family of a student who was stabbed at a school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, will file a civil suit and provide full cooperation to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) in its appeal against the case.

95faa08ac167436b: PARIS: Pope Leo XIV on Friday warned against losing humanity in a "paradise of machines", after church bells rang and thousands gathered to welcome him to France amid worldwide concern over the dangers of artificial intelligence.

"If we are to avoid losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines invading and conditioning our daily lives, there is an urgent need for education in ethical discernment," Leo said after President Emmanuel Macron welcomed him to the presidential palace, on the first of four days in the country.

On the first official papal trip in 18 years to a proudly secular country that has since 1901 separated church and state, the pope also stressed that "authentic secularity" should not exclude religion.

It "consists not in excluding religion from the public sphere or from education, but in striving to ensure that the state and religious institutions maintain dialogue and join forces in the service of the common good," the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics said.
Politicians have in recent years invoked France's brand of secularism to justify bans on religious symbols including Muslim women's attire in public spaces and schools.
France is just seven months away from the first round of its presidential election to replace Macron, with the anti-immigration far right eyeing its best chance at seizing power in the vote.
'Sense of peace'

After France passed legislation in June granting some adult patients the right to assisted dying, the first US pontiff said he was concerned by trends "that risk turning science and technology into profit-driven ventures promoting genetic manipulation, surrogacy, the trade in human organs or the possibility of arranging one's own death".

The pope, whose paternal grandmother was born in France, urged the European nation to remain a "tireless champion of peace" worldwide, as Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine drags into its fifth year.

Macron and his wife Brigitte earlier greeted the 71-year-old pope at the airport, where a red carpet was rolled out on the tarmac, as he marked the first official trip by a head of the Vatican since Pope Benedict XVI in September 2008.
"I'm travelling to France, as to anywhere else in the world, as a follower of Jesus Christ wanting to proclaim peace, the peace of Christ throughout the world," Pope Leo told reporters on the plane.
He said the message was "particularly important" at the current time.
A million people are expected at events across Paris during the first two days of his trip.
The high point of the apostolic journey will be a giant mass on Saturday, led by the pontiff at Place de la Concorde and adjoining Champs-Elysees.

Pope Leo will also visit Lourdes, a pilgrimage site for Christians worldwide where he will privately meet victims of clerical sex abuse, and Metz, near the German border, where he is to further speak about peace in Europe.
"The pope's visit gives me a sense of peace in a troubled world," said Andree Estienne, 76, adding she could not wait to attend the mass on the Champs-Elysees.
"I don't think I will experience anything of this scale again in my lifetime."

09d5a977ab09379e: HOUSTON: Washington's talk of a possible ban on diesel exports is widening the gap between US crude oil futures and the global Brent benchmark, a signal that markets expect US refiners to process less crude oil if their diesel output gets stuck at home.

While that may bring some immediate relief to high domestic diesel prices, which this week hit a record US$6.528 a gallon and stirred a political uproar, the bigger discount for domestic crude futures could be a double-edged omen: an indicator of higher gasoline prices to come, while in the longer term diesel prices could also begin rising again.

As investors price in a scenario where diesel gets stranded in the US, West Texas Intermediate crude futures traded as much as US$12.02 a barrel under Brent futures on Thursday, their largest discount since May 6, according to LSEG data.
Analysts say US refiners could cut their crude runs by as much as 12 per cent if diesel exports are banned, with key storage hubs likely to fill up within a month.
The US is the world's largest diesel exporter, with net exports of about 1.2 million barrels per day, versus production of 5.1 million bpd, according to Morgan Stanley.

These exports have partially plugged the gap from lost Middle East barrels while the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed. Diesel supplies have also dwindled from Russia, which has repeatedly imposed export bans of its own to tackle shortages that followed Ukrainian drone attacks on its oil refineries.

Wood Mackenzie analysts, in a note on Thursday, said a diesel export ban would redirect a 700,000 bpd oversupply of diesel and gasoil into storage, effectively filling Gulf Coast inventories to maximum capacity in just over a month.

That would force US refiners to cut crude runs by more than 2 million bpd, Wood Mackenzie estimated, to prevent inventories from exceeding capacity — a reduction of 12 per cent of US refinery crude runs at current rates.
The prospects for a US diesel export ban remain uncertain.

The White House on Wednesday denied media reports it was preparing for a 90-day diesel export ban, and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said a ban would not bring surging prices under control. On Tuesday, however, President Donald Trump said he backed a ban.

In the meantime, Wright has contacted executives at several major American refiners in recent days to gauge support for voluntary restraint on diesel exports, as the Trump administration searches for an alternative to a short-term ban, according to three people familiar with the discussions.
RECORD DIESEL PRICES STIR CALLS FOR EXPORT BAN

Driving the demand for a US export ban is a surge in diesel prices, which have hit records in both the US and Europe. On Thursday, US prices remained elevated at US$6.514 a gallon, according to the AAA, as the US war with Iran disrupts global supplies.

That could spell trouble for Trump's Republican Party in the November midterm elections, by fuelling inflation and putting a particularly heavy burden on farmers, one of the party's key constituencies.
The Iran war is complicating the conundrum in the US oil sector in another way: by boosting shipping costs.

A rise in the discount for US crude relative to European crude, known as the WTI-Brent spread, typically boosts demand for US oil and increases exports, as traders can make a profit through arbitrage by selling it abroad. But that depends on shipping costs.
Rising freight rates and tight vessel availability have dimmed demand for US exports and contributed to the widening WTI-Brent spread, Georgios Sakellariou, freight analyst at Signal Maritime, said.
While the WTI-Brent spread has been trending wider in the third quarter, US crude exports have not risen significantly, according to data from ship tracker Kpler.

Shipping crude from the US Gulf Coast to Asian markets on a very large crude carrier currently costs around US$50 million in freight, according to Signal Maritime, compared with US$16 million before the Iran war broke out and drove up war risk premiums.

The discount that a barrel of US crude would need versus a European barrel to offset shipping costs was previously around minus US$4 a barrel, according to Bob Yawger, director of energy futures at Mizuho. It is now likely double that, at minus US$8, due to surging freight rates, Yawger said.

"International crude is carrying a higher scarcity and logistics premium, while US barrels are struggling to clear abroad at current transportation costs," said Shohruh Zukhritdinov, chief executive at oil trading firm NitrolOil.

The WTI-Brent spread has traded exclusively at a US$4 discount or wider since July 7, according to LSEG. Yet US crude exports have remained relatively flat month over month, rising only 45,000 barrels per day from July to August, at 3.72 million bpd, according to Kpler.

On a three-month average basis, US crude exports for September are currently on track to fall for the third consecutive month to their lowest since before the Iran war broke out in February, according to Kpler.
"A wide paper spread is an invitation to test the arbitrage, not proof that the arbitrage is open," said Zukhritdinov.

One more thing
This scientist rewarmed and studied pieces of his friend’s cryopreserved brain

L. Stephen Coles’s brain sits in a vat at a storage facility in Arizona. It has been held there at a temperature of around −146°C for more than a decade, largely undisturbed. Before he died in 2014, Coles had the brain frozen with an ambitious goal in mind: reanimation.
His friend, cryobiologist Greg Fahy, believes it could be revived one day. But other experts are less optimistic.
Still, Fahy’s research could lead to new ways to study the brain. And using cryopreservation for organ transplantation is becoming a viable reality.

b6c7fec985520754: HONG KONG/LONDON: The dollar fell on Friday but was on track for its second consecutive weekly gain on rising rate hike bets, while the yen rallied after Japan said Tokyo and Washington remain committed to the stance behind July's joint intervention.

The euro rose 0.2 per cent to US$1.141 as energy prices fell, moderating wagers on Federal Reserve rate increases, but was on track for a third weekly decline after touching a two-month low on Thursday.

Sterling rose 0.3 per cent to US$1.326, boosted by hawkish comments from Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey. Yet it remained close to a three-month low and was set for its second straight weekly one per cent fall.

Markets have aggressively repriced the US interest rate trajectory after the Federal Reserve tightened policy last week. Robust economic data, fresh energy supply concerns and a chorus of hawkish Fed speakers have further strengthened that conviction.
A bond selloff, which sent long-dated US Treasury yields to their highest in more than 20 years, also gave the greenback a leg up.
The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, climbed to a two-month high on Thursday and was set for its first back-to-back weekly increase since June.
However, it gave back some of its recent gains and fell 0.3 per cent on Friday to 100.96.

"Whilst the dollar should get a bid from higher yields, there are still ongoing, lingering concerns around the US fiscal position, the unpredictability of US policy making," said Khoon Goh, head of Asia research at ANZ.
"I think that's why the dollar has really struggled to continue to rally, even though yields continue to increase."

Oil prices eased on Friday on signs of easing supply disruptions and hopes of progress in talks between the US and Iran. Yet crude remained close to a one-week high as a Houthi missile attack on Saudi Arabia kept Middle East tensions high.
YEN STRENGTHENS AS JAPAN STEPS UP INTERVENTION WARNINGS
The Japanese yen bounced 0.8 per cent from three-week lows to fetch 157.65 per dollar.

The currency rose after Japan's Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said US President Donald Trump raised concern about yen weakness during a summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi earlier this week.

Katayama said this reaffirmed the shared US-Japan stance behind July's joint intervention, adding she and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent would stay in close contact as policymakers stepped up warnings over renewed yen weakness.

"Katayama's comment ... clearly underlines the ongoing efforts in Tokyo to portray the efforts to stem yen weakness as a continued joint strategy," said senior MUFG currency strategist Derek Halpenny.
"That certainly reinforces the possibility that additional intervention could again include the US."
Still, the yen was on track for a second weekly fall, after markets judged the Bank of Japan's rate hike last week to a 31-year high and its latest guidance as insufficiently hawkish.

Elsewhere, the offshore yuan was flat at 6.721 per dollar, as a Trump-Xi summit in Washington showed no signs of breakthroughs at a closed-door meeting on thorny issues such as AI, trade, Taiwan and the Iran war.
The Australian dollar rose 0.3 per cent to US$0.703. The Reserve Bank of Australia is expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points to a nearly 15-year high of 4.60 per cent next week

141c3b9b7b6d0a3f: NAGOYA: Towering teenager Zhang Zhanshuo became the first swimmer in history to win seven golds at a single Asian Games on Friday, as North Korea's women set yet more world records in weightlifting.
China's Zhang, 19, scorched to the men's 400m freestyle title in Tokyo in a Games-record 3min 41.28sec.
He sat on the lane divider after the race and slowly counted off on his fingers all seven medals he had won.
Zhang also won individual golds in the 200m, 800m and 1,500m freestyle events, as well as three relays.

Their 13-year-old phenomenon Yu Zidi was the undoubted superstar, taking home three individual golds and all in Games-record times.
Not be outdone, Japan's 17-year-old Shin Ohashi shattered the men's 200m breaststroke world record on Thursday.
Swimming, equestrian and diving are taking place in Tokyo, but the city of Nagoya and the wider Aichi prefecture are the main Games host.

d0bb7c564a59863e: KUALA LUMPUR: Actor Adam Shahz has hit back at critics online who accused him of being ungrateful for turning down low-paying acting roles, insisting his stance is rooted in reality.
The 46-year-old actor — whose real name is Nor Shah Azli Abdol Ghani — said earning RM300 to RM400 a day might sound like a decent sum on paper, but it paints a misleading picture.
"The TV dramas I feature in often take two to three months to wrap up," he explained.
"Big lump-sum payouts are reserved for lead actors. Supporting cast members like me are usually paid by the day."
Adam pointed out that supporting actors rarely appear in every scene.
In a 30-episode series, a character might only pop up in five episodes, with scenes shot weeks apart rather than back-to-back.
"If an actor shoots three days one month and two days the next at RM600 a day, they bring home RM1,800 the first month and RM1,200 the second," he said.
"Once you break down the actual numbers, it's clear no one is living lavishly. You're taking home less than RM2,000 a month."
He added that poor pay forces many actors to seek alternative income streams, such as starting side businesses with friends.
"We all have bills to pay and mouths to feed. When acting alone doesn't cover the essentials, you have no choice but to juggle multiple jobs just to make ends meet."
eff5ead055d6394a: PETALING JAYA: A constitutional law expert said it was wrong to accuse the attorney-general of interfering in the Negeri Sembilan crisis as he is the federation’s most senior legal adviser.
Aziz Bari said Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar has to issue a statement on the matter.

“He has to put his position forward because the public are waiting, eager and anxious to know whether it is right or wrong,” he told FMT, referring to the constitutional crisis sparked by the attempted removal of Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Negeri Sembilan’s ruler.

On Sept 17, the Attorney-General's Chambers rejected a proclamation purporting to remove Tuanku Muhriz as the Yang Dipertuan Besar, along with a subsequent announcement by the then executive committee affirming it.
The AGC said the proclamation was invalid, and that the menteri besar and the exco members had no unilateral power to remove the ruler.

On Wednesday, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim also criticised menteri besar Ismail Lasim and the former exco over several matters involving the royal institution which had sparked controversy in the state.

Today, Negeri Sembilan’s four undangs, including three whose appointments are disputed, and the Tunku Besar of Tampin urged Anwar and the AGC not to interfere in the state's affairs, particularly in matters concerning their constitutional prerogatives.
At a press conference in Seremban, they asserted that Articles 10 and 11 of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution 1959 conferred them with exclusive powers to appoint and remove the state’s ruler.

Aziz said that while Articles 10 and 11 of the Negeri Sembilan constitution gave the chieftains the exclusive authority to appoint and remove the Yang Dipertuan Besar, the said provisions “cannot be read and interpreted in isolation”.
He said this was because the chieftains are "part of a larger community".
“Just because you have an exclusive right within your compound or your house does not mean you can simply do whatever you want without considering how it would eventually affect your neighbours.
“We live in a community, and that is part of the constitution,” he said.
He also said the constitution - federal or state - envisages and deals with a crisis-free situation.

However, the Negeri Sembilan crisis has reached a stage “where the system is upside down and there is a conflict”, and a solution could not be expected to be found within the mechanism or framework of the constitution.
“In other words, it’s quite futile to argue solely on the basis of the provisions, especially when the players are now racing to push the button, as it were,” he said.

On the argument by the undangs, whom he labelled as “arrogant”, that the so-called interference by Anwar constituted a breach of the prime minister’s oath of office under the Sixth Schedule of the Federal Constitution, a breach of trust under Article 71(1) and (2), and a violation of the principle of federalism, Aziz said the constitution stipulates limits on federal powers and, at the same time, provides safeguards for the states, being the original entities that formed the federation.
“But the problem now is whether we are seeing the proper way of exercising state power," he said.
"I think the federal government, or the federal authorities, have a moral responsibility to keep the federation intact.”
7a40179a18f00d05: PETALING JAYA: Pakar undang-undang perlembagaan berkata adalah tidak wajar untuk menuduh peguam negara campur tangan dalam krisis di Negeri Sembilan kerana beliau merupakan penasihat undang-undang tertinggi Persekutuan.

Hari ini, empat Undang Negeri Sembilan, termasuk tiga yang pelantikannya dipertikaikan, serta Tunku Besar Tampin menggesa Anwar dan AGC supaya tidak campur tangan dalam urusan negeri, khususnya perkara berkaitan bidang kuasa perlembagaan mereka.

Pada sidang media di Seremban, mereka menegaskan bahawa Perkara 10 dan 11 Undang-Undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri Sembilan 1959 memberikan mereka kuasa eksklusif untuk melantik dan menurunkan takhta pemerintah negeri.

Aziz berkata walaupun Perkara 10 dan 11 Perlembagaan Negeri Sembilan memberikan Undang kuasa eksklusif untuk melantik dan menurunkan takhta Yang Dipertuan Besar, peruntukan berkenaan 'tidak boleh dibaca dan ditafsirkan secara berasingan'.
Katanya, ini kerana Undang merupakan 'sebahagian daripada masyarakat yang lebih besar'.

“Hanya kerana anda mempunyai hak eksklusif dalam kawasan atau rumah anda, itu tidak bermakna anda boleh melakukan apa sahaja tanpa mengambil kira bagaimana tindakan itu akhirnya akan menjejaskan jiran anda.
“Kita hidup dalam sebuah masyarakat dan itu adalah sebahagian daripada perlembagaan,” katanya.
Beliau turut berkata perlembagaan, sama ada di peringkat Persekutuan atau negeri, dirangka untuk keadaan tanpa krisis dan menangani situasi sedemikian.

Bagaimanapun, krisis di Negeri Sembilan kini sudah mencapai tahap 'di mana sistemnya terbalik dan berlaku konflik' dan penyelesaian tidak boleh diharapkan daripada peruntukan atau kerangka perlembagaan.
“Dalam erti kata lain, agak sia-sia untuk berhujah semata-mata berdasarkan peruntukan, terutama apabila pihak terbabit kini berlumba-lumba untuk bertindak, boleh dikatakan begitu,” katanya.

Mengenai hujah Undang yang disifatkannya sebagai 'angkuh' apabila mendakwa campur tangan Anwar adalah pelanggaran sumpah jawatan perdana menteri di bawah Jadual Keenam Perlembagaan Persekutuan, melanggar amanah di bawah Perkara 71(1) dan (2), serta konsep federalisme, Aziz berkata perlembagaan menetapkan batas kuasa Persekutuan dan pada masa sama menyediakan perlindungan kepada negeri-negeri sebagai entiti asal yang membentuk Persekutuan.
“Tetapi masalahnya sekarang ialah sama ada kita sedang melihat cara yang betul dalam melaksanakan kuasa negeri,” katanya.
“Saya fikir kerajaan Persekutuan atau pihak berkuasa Persekutuan mempunyai tanggungjawab moral untuk memastikan Persekutuan kekal utuh.”

e7a9f2d4214692dc: Gravity Linux is a newly announced distro targeting newer Apple Silicon Macs, and its first experimental alpha already boots an accelerated desktop on the M4 Mac mini. The project homepage says: "Gravity Linux is a Fedora remix that brings a fast, modern Linux desktop to Apple Silicon – built in the open, by people like you." If this sounds familiar, the About page explains: "Gravity Linux was initially forked from Asahi Linux over differences in policy, namely regarding LLM use. We have tremendous respect for the Asahi Linux project and emphasize our shared goal of running Linux on Apple Silicon." There's already an early alpha release for the M4 Mac mini, a model launched in October 2024 just days after the company announced the M4 iMac. It includes GPU acceleration with OpenGL ES 3.0 and OpenGL 3.3 support, but is explicitly aimed at developers rather than daily use. HDMI output works, but USB-C displays, USB4, Thunderbolt, and suspend do not, while power management remains incomplete. In terms of hardware generations, this puts Gravity ahead of Asahi Linux. As The Register reported earlier this month, Asahi has only recently added preliminary M3 support, for now without graphics acceleration. The comparison is not exact, however: Gravity's M4 release is an early developer alpha, while Asahi is a longer-established project supporting a much broader range of hardware. Apple, meanwhile, has already moved on: The Reg reported on the first M6-based Macs last month, nearly three years after the company launched its "scary fast" M3 systems. The Reg reported on the new Asahi Linux project in March 2022, and tried it out later the same month. However, Asahi has since lost several prominent contributors. Project lead Hector Martin resigned in February 2025. A week later, the leader of the GPU effort, known only as "Asahi Lina," also quit. As we mentioned later that year, in August 2025, the leader of the GPU driver effort, Alyssa Rosenzweig, left the project. She had already, in her own words, passed the reins on to her other Arm GPU drivers that April. As her resume [PDF] shows, she's been working for Intel since then. Gravity attributes much of its rapid progress to a development method that Asahi explicitly prohibits. Project lead Cody Ho previously worked at both Apple and OpenAI, and has published a two-part account of using coding agents for Apple Silicon reverse engineering. On August 3, Ho published the first part of "I Came, I Prompted, I Left," describing the construction of a custom hypervisor for newer Apple Silicon. The second part, published on September 15, explains how he and co-developer Niklas Sheth built an M4 GPU driver in about a month. Ho says much of the work was performed through largely unattended LLM loops. This is one of the sharpest differences between Gravity Linux and Asahi Linux. Ho and Sheth are reverse-engineering Apple's hardware with the assistance of AI tools, while the Asahi project has a Generative AI (LLM) Policy that says "we broadly forbid the use of generative AI tooling for material contributions to Asahi Linux." Gravity's LLM Use and Clean-Room Policy permits such tools but attempts to contain the legal risks through separation. It states: "If in any session your LLM has looked at any disassembly, decompilation, or other protected implementation details of an Apple component, you must consider yourself tainted with respect to that component." This does not mean nobody involved looks at Apple binaries. Ho says that while developing the hypervisor, he used an LLM to disassemble Apple's proprietary SPTM component. That made him ineligible to write the corresponding clean-room implementation, so the knowledge had to be documented and handed to someone who had not seen the protected material. Ho and Sheth say the GPU work followed a stricter route, using hardware traces, live probing and self-written shaders without inspecting Apple binaries. They also acknowledge benefiting from Asahi's earlier M1 and M2 work and using its existing userspace API. The result is nevertheless striking: Gravity's first alpha brings an accelerated Linux desktop to an M4 Mac mini, and Ho credits LLMs with helping the pair achieve in weeks work that would ordinarily take far longer. But the code still requires extensive testing, human review, and refactoring before it can be upstreamed. Gravity's developers warn that its kernel driver may have to wait for Asahi's M1 and M2 driver to land upstream first. Gravity has therefore produced an intriguing demonstration of what AI-assisted reverse engineering can do, rather than a controlled experiment proving that Asahi's policy is what held it back. ®

9c67b06227ae2b17: PARIS: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner delayed his return to the courts when he withdrew from next week's China Open in Beijing on Friday, having been out of action since his Wimbledon title in July due to a right knee injury.

"I won't be able to play in Beijing this year. My knee is not there where I would like it to be, and I'm not ready to compete yet, but I will do everything possible to be there as soon as I can," the Italian defending champion said on X.
The five-time Grand Slam winner has not played since winning Wimbledon on July 12, pulling out of the US Open last month.
Sinner, 25, had been dominating the 2026 season with an impressive record of 44 wins against three losses and six titles won, including Wimbledon.
However, he suffered a major disappointment at the French Open, where he arrived as the overwhelming favourite but crashed out in the second round after suffering in a heatwave.
The absence of the tour's top player in Beijing increases the chances for his closest rival, Alexander Zverev, to move to the top of the ATP rankings for the first time by the end of the season.

31d17940f9929b22: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Bar will challenge the Federal Territories Pardons Board's decision and advice concerning Datuk Seri Najib Razak's second pardon, which allows him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest.

Its president Anand Raj said the Bar, through its solicitors, would challenge the decision and advice concerning the second pardon while maintaining its appeal against the board's 2024 decision to reduce Najib's prison sentence and fine.

"The Malaysian Bar will, through its solicitors, challenge the decision and advice of the Pardons Board concerning the Second Pardon, while maintaining its appeal in relation to the Pardons Board's decision and advice on the First Pardon," he said in a statement today.
The Bar also questioned the need for a public fundraiser to pay Najib's RM50 million fine, pointing out that more than RM114 million in cash seized in 2018 had been returned to his representative.
Anand said RM114,164,393.44 seized during police raids in May 2018 was returned in June 2021 after forfeiture proceedings were dismissed.
He added that jewellery, handbags and spectacles were returned to Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, while watches were returned to Najib by June 2022.
Given the assets that had been returned, Anand questioned why Umno needed to raise public funds to pay the fine.
"Such a public fundraiser may also involve other legal considerations," he said.
He also questioned reports that most of Najib's assets had been frozen, saying the returned funds appeared sufficient to cover the fine without public contributions.
"This is not clear, nor have any details been made available publicly," he said, referring to whether any other unseized assets remained frozen.
On the legal effect of a pardon, Anand said it did not amount to an exoneration of guilt.
"Neither a pardon, a reprieve, nor a respite constitutes an exoneration of guilt or removal of wrongdoing. They do not 'wipe the slate clean' of the prior conviction," he said.

He also cited High Court judge Alice Loke's ruling last December that Malaysian law makes no provision for house arrest, a position he said had previously been confirmed by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
"From our research to date, there appear to be no standard operating procedures or guidelines in place for 'house arrests'.
"A whole new ecosystem of rules and procedures would be required to operationalise 'house arrests'," he said.
The Bar called on the Pardons Board and the Prime Minister's Department to declassify and publish the minutes of the board's meetings concerning both of Najib's pardons.
It also called for full disclosure of the conditions of the house arrest, including monitoring protocols, enforcement authorities and additional costs to taxpayers.

Citing a joint statement issued by civil society groups and individuals, including Datuk Ambiga Sreenevasan and Maria Chin Abdullah, the Bar renewed its call for a freedom of information framework to ensure public access to such details.
Anand also raised concerns about the precedent that the decision could set.
"The Pardons Board will now receive many more petitions for 'house arrest'.
"Clear and objective criteria, made known in advance, are crucial to avoid any perceptions of preferential treatment for Najib.
"On what basis may any other convict or prisoner seek a similar pardon, reprieve or respite?" he said.

On Sept 18, the Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine.

Najib, 73, was convicted in 2020 of abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million from SRC International. He was initially sentenced to 12 years in prison and fined RM210 million.
In 2024, the Pardons Board reduced his prison sentence to 6 years and his fine to RM50 million.
He is also seeking a stay of execution of a separate 15-year prison sentence and RM11.38 billion fine in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case.

5d88e1a95a9bd4cf: PARIS, Sept 25 — The four main European football leagues — the English Premier League, Spain’s La Liga, Italy’s Serie A and Germany’s Bundesliga — called today for a reform of Fifa.

The sport’s governing body has been mired in crisis since the revelation of a plan, since shelved, to create a commercial company Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would be open to private investors.

“Fundamental governance reform is essential to restore clear constitutional boundaries within Fifa, including confidence that individual disciplinary matters remain demonstrably insulated from political interference,” the four leagues wrote in a statement sent to AFP.
“We are speaking up together, as founding members of European Leagues and the World Leagues Association, because we understand how Fifa’s relentless expansionism affects everyone.”

The statement comes just days after Fifa president Gianni Infantino — who has come under fire since the FFE plan to bring private investment into the men’s and women’s World Cups — proposed “a consultation” of the national federations in order to reform the body’s governance.

“The Fifa president has now acknowledged the need for reform, but it is not enough for surface-level, process changes to be explored in the aftermath of FFE,” stated the four main European leagues, who went on to describe the project as “one of the biggest abuses of power in Fifa’s history”.
The four leagues, however, steered away from putting all the blame on Infantino’s shoulders.
“Fifa’s governance problem goes far beyond the role of one individual,” they said.
They propose the creation of a permanent body representing national associations, leagues, clubs and players, from across men’s and women’s football.
“This new body must be fully informed about new initiatives and have a meaningful role in Fifa’s decision-making process,” they added.

“Any major Fifa proposal must begin with a clearly defined rationale, supporting evidence and an independent assessment, published in advance of any decision, covering players, clubs, leagues and supporters, and evaluating the impact on all stakeholders and the development of football.”
They also called for the protection of Fifa’s role “as regulator and guardian of the game” from its commercial activities.
The four leagues put a call out for candidates for the Fifa presidency who will endorse their principles “within the first 100 days of the next presidential mandate”.
For now, Infantino is the sole candidate for the Fifa presidential election scheduled for March 18, 2027, with the submission of candidacies open until November 18.
Uefa, alongside North American body Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), issued a no-holds-barred joint letter against Infantino in August.
“Leadership in football is not a possession. It is not about holding — or demanding — power to be held,” they wrote.

However, Infantino is not without friends — 2034 World Cup hosts Saudi Arabia came out in support last month, with African football’s governing body CAF and South America’s Conmebol also supportive. — AFP
adfa9a0566057313: KUALA LUMPUR: Persatuan Insurans Hayat Malaysia (LIAM) meminta kerajaan mengecualikan skim insurans pekerja berkelompok daripada cukai perkhidmatan 8% di bawah Belanjawan 2027.
